en: to go on; to happen; carry on
to make; to let; to allow; why (we mek = why); so that
to beg; please (mi a beg yu)
a chance; a break (gi mi a bly)
trick, fool someone — /tr/ is affricated in Patois and written chr-, as in chrai, chrut: Duon mek dem chrik yu, don't let them trick you
thing, object, matter — the everyday form; raising the register restores the English th: 'ting' bikom 'thing', 'ting' becomes 'thing'
foolish, silly: Dem tink se wi fuul, they think we're foolish; also to fool someone: Duon mek dem fuul yu, don't let them fool you
wouldn't — the negated modal, positive wuda: Ef yu did lisn, yu wudn ina problem, if you had listened you wouldn't be in trouble
couldn't — the negated modal; the course's positive form is kuda: Mi did waan kom bot mi kudn, I wanted to come but I couldn't
the light, and by extension the electricity supply: wen di lait gaan, when the power went
care — chiefly in tek kier, to take care: Tek kier a yuself, take care of yourself
yet, so far; goes with the negator no: di shap no open yet, the shop isn't open yet
mathematics, maths as a school subject: shi a tiich matimatiks, she teaches maths
this (the near one); demonstrative: Dis a di bes mango, this is the best mango
do; one bare form for every person and tense: Wa yu a du?, what are you doing?
elders, the older people you owe respect: respek yu eldas, respect your elders
one who wants; proverb only: Wanti wanti kyaan getti, those who want can't get
call — shout for, or telephone: No figet fi kaal mi, don't forget to call me
Patois, the Jamaican language: Mi waan fi laan Patwa, I want to learn Patois
from, marking origin: rege myuuzik kom fram Jamieka, reggae comes from Jamaica
to, before the person: Lisn tu mi gud, listen to me well; also spelled to
to think; Patois has no 'th' sound: mi laik ou yu tingk, I like how you think
negative progressive, no + a before the verb: Mi naa go, I'm not going
over: jomp ova di fens, jump over the fence; kom ova, come over to visit
morning: Mi drink ti evri maanin, I drink tea every morning; also mawnin
in kuul dong, to calm down, take it easy: Kuul dong, man, calm down, man
send: Sen di pikni go kaal di dakta, send the child to go call the doctor
to fly; a flai = is flying, a marking the progressive: di jankro a flai hai
worth, of a value; no 'is' needed: it wort wan touzn dala, it's worth $1000
to grow; verbs take no -s: ganja gruo inna di ils, ganja grows in the hills
frighten, scare: Dopi nuo uu fi fraitn, the ghost knows whom to frighten
taller, comparative of taal; no 'am': mi taala dan yu, I'm taller than you
finger; no -s plural after a number: mi hab ten finga, I have ten fingers
dinner, the evening meal: Wi a nyam dina nou, we are eating dinner now
fall; the ordinary verb for rain: Rien a faal tide, it's raining today
to sting; bare verb carries the past: wan waas sting mi, a wasp stung me
ball, the thing you throw or kick: trow di baal gi mi, throw me the ball
full: Mi beli ful, my belly is full; as a verb, to fill: ful baskit
tag question at sentence end: eh? right? — Di konsert did gud, iihn?
don't; negator opening a command: Duon tach dat!, don't touch that!
preposition: behind, at the back of — baka di bush, behind the bush
that (the far one); demonstrative: Duon tach dat, don't touch that
egg; the plural takes no ending: Bai wan dazn eg, buy a dozen eggs
pot for cooking: Put di pat pan di faiya, put the pot on the fire
show, performance: Di shuo a go staat, the show is going to start
dog; plural with dem: Di daag dem a baak, the dogs are barking
hard, difficult — no copula needed: Di tes aad, the test is hard
mean, intend: Mi neva miin fi bex yu, I didn't mean to upset you
nothing but, plain, only: soso rais, plain rice and nothing else
football, soccer: Dem a plie futbaal, they are playing football
hard, with effort: Wi wok haad evri die, we work hard every day
bark, what a dog does: Di daag dem a baak, the dogs are barking
meeting: Im neva kom a di miitn, he didn't come to the meeting
register, level of speech: Raiz di rejista, raise the register
whole, entire: di huol pat, the whole pot; as a verb, to hold
alright, fine: Evriting aarait nou, everything is alright now
late: Yu a mek mi liet fi wok, you're making me late for work
win — no past ending: ef yu win di moni, if you won the money
early: A tide di bos kom orli, it's today the bus comes early
to turn; ton op = turn up: ton op di myuuzik, turn the music up
sweet, tasty; doubled as swiit-swiit it means 'really sweet'
sentence-final softener, 'you hear?': Tek kier a yuself, yaa
basket: Wan wan koko ful baskit, one by one fills the basket
fence: di daag jomp ova di fens, the dog jumped over the fence
o'clock, used in telling the hour: a six aklak, at six o'clock
Sunday: Wi go a chorch pan Sondi, we go to church on Sunday
glass, a drinking glass: wan glaas a wata, a glass of water
picture, photo: Mek mi si di pikcha, let me see the picture
merry, in high spirits: Chikin meri, haak de nier (proverb)
hawk, the bird of prey: Chikin meri, haak de nier (proverb)
gate, the one in a yard or fence: shet di giet, shut the gate
cocoyam, a starchy root: Wan wan koko ful baskit (proverb)
every, each; before a singular noun: evri die, every day
plate: pluralised with dem — di pliet dem, the plates
about, concerning: Wi taak bout it, we talked about it
child — the high-register form; deep Patois says pikni
busy; adjectives need no 'is' or 'am': mi bizi, I'm busy
key; keys (no -s; plural comes from dem or the context)
week: Sevn die inna wan wiik, seven days in a week
rest, take a break: Mi niid fi res, I need to rest
arrive, reach: Mi riich a nain, I arrived at nine
happen, take place: wen it hapn, when it happened
straight, upright: tan op strait, stand up straight
ready: Wi riedi fi go nou, we're ready to go now
quick; quickly (one form for both — no -ly ending)
smell: Di fuud smel gud, the food smells good
cost: Umoch it kaas?, how much does it cost?
test, exam: Di tes aad, the test is hard
to pass, to hand (something to someone)
